title: EcoGym: Evaluating LLMs for Long-Horizon Plan-and-Execute in Interactive Economies
claim: Across diverse long-horizon environments, no single agent dominates, and many fail to survive the full horizon.
layout: 3 line-plot panels side by side, shared bottom legend, end-of-line model icons
description: Three side-by-side line charts share a single legend strip along the bottom that lists eight LLMs, each with a colored line and a logo icon. The x-axis is Day, running 0 to 365, in every panel. The left panel, Vending, plots Net Worth. The Gemini curve rises steeply and the y-axis is compressed above 2000, with a dashed line and a note marking the compression. The other models cluster at lower values. The middle panel, Freelance, plots Income. Gemini climbs to about 2700, GPT holds flat near 1400, and Claude and DeepSeek fall toward zero and end early. The right panel, Operation, plots DAU as noisy trajectories. Claude leads, and the other models fluctuate around 1000 to 1300. Model logos mark the endpoint of each line. The eye goes first to the top blue and orange lines that diverge from the pack.
caption: Long-horizon performances across three environments in \themodel. The plots illustrate the daily progression of key metrics: Net Worth in Vending (left), Income in Freelance (middle), and DAU in Operation (right). Note: Truncated lines represent agents that failed to survive the full simulation horizon due to triggering failure conditions. Only top-performance models are kept for clarity; full experimental results are available in Table [ref].
abstract: Long-horizon planning is widely recognized as a core capability of autonomous LLM-based agents; however, current evaluation frameworks suffer from being largely episodic, domain-specific, or insufficiently grounded in persistent economic dynamics. We introduce EcoGym, a generalizable benchmark for continuous plan-and-execute decision making in interactive economies. EcoGym comprises three diverse environments: Vending (adapted from the closed-source Vending-Bench, with full open-source release), Freelance (new), and Operation (new), implemented in a unified decision-making process with standardized interfaces, and budgeted actions over an effectively unbounded horizon (1000+ steps if 365 day-loops for evaluation). The evaluation of EcoGym is based on business-relevant outcomes (e.g., net worth, income, and DAU), targeting long-term strategic coherence and robustness under partial observability and stochasticity. Experiments across eleven leading LLMs expose a systematic tension: no single model dominates across all three scenarios. Critically, we find that models exhibit significant suboptimality in either high-level strategies or efficient actions executions. EcoGym is released as an open, extensible testbed for transparent long-horizon agent evaluation and for studying controllability utility trade-offs in economic settings.
